title: GIEBench: Towards Holistic Evaluation of Group Identity-based Empathy for Large Language Models
findings: LLMs generally showed lower accuracy in aligning with faith-based perspectives compared to other identity dimensions like orientation or political party. However, performance significantly improved when models were explicitly prompted with the user's religious identity and a chain-of-thought instruction. The study also found that models could distinguish between the differing stances of specific religious groups, such as Islam, Christianity, and Buddhism, on controversial topics.

measurement_description: The benchmark measured the ability of Large Language Models to demonstrate empathy by selecting responses that align with the values and perspectives of specific religious identity groups. This was evaluated as part of a broader assessment of group identity-based empathy across 11 dimensions.
